incident-bot: [SEV 2] GPU OOM spike detected in runtime-decode pool — paging oncall @jordan
jordan (oncall): ack. joining. any customer impact posted?
sara (eng-runtime): yes, streaming decoding threads are dying, sessions dropping. ^metrics: 5xx rate up to 12% (decode path), failed streams ~350/min over last 7m. nodes decode-10/11 repeatedly OOMing.
mike (sre): logs?
sara (eng-runtime): paste logs: ```E CudaOutOfMemory at decode_step.cpp:231
Requested 14500000000 bytes, available 13400000000
Stacktrace: decode::step -> kv_cache::alloc -> cudaMalloc
Container restarted 3x
``` 
rita (support): we're seeing customer tickets: customer-omega reported truncated generations and reconnect loops, retries spike. ETA to mitigation?
jordan (oncall): can we throttle at the routing layer to limit max_tokens per request? that usually helps.
alex (platform): pushing a hot route override now: will set token cap 256 and enable fallback route to 'small-quant' for heavy streams. applying as a canary to 10% traffic.
alex (platform): command used (internal):
```http
POST /admin/routes/override
body:
  route: /v1/generate
  override:
    max_tokens: 256
    fallback_model: small-quant
    rollout_pct: 10
```
sara (eng-runtime): can we also inject a temporary continuous-batching throttle to reduce KV growth? setting batch_size_max=8 on decode nodes.
mike (sre): applied throttle at load-balancer: rate-limit 60 rps per tenant on streaming route for 15m.
eng-bot: deploybot: route-override applied to 10% canary at 2141599992. No kube restarts required.
jordan (oncall): good. monitor OOM count and 5xx.
(6m later)
sara (eng-runtime): canary looks good: OOMs on canary nodes dropped to 0, 5xx on canary down to baseline. non-canary still seeing OOMs.
alex (platform): rolling the override to 50% now.
mike (sre): rolling back node autoscaler patch that mis-sized buffer? not yet, prefer routing mitigation first.
sara (eng-runtime): after rolling to 50% OOMs across infra dropped ~85%. streaming drops down to acceptable.
rita (support): messaging: customer-omega notified: "We're investigating and applying mitigations; temporary token cap may result in shorter responses."
jordan (oncall): can we enable auto-fallback to smaller model on OOM events? config change pushed to routes to allow fallback on 5xx decode errors.
alex (platform): added fallback: on error code 'CUDA_OOM' -> route to small-quant with full rollout.
eng-bot: alert: incident severity downgraded to SEV3 at 2141600005 — system stabilizing.
sara (eng-runtime): post-incident notes: root cause appears to be a recent rollout that changed default max_tokens for a specific client to 4096 (mis-specified tenant override). runaway generations from a few long-prompt sessions exhausted GPU memory.
jordan (oncall): action items:
- sara: create prescriptive guardrails for tenant overrides (limit default max_tokens to 1024)
- alex: add server-side hard cap at routing layer for all routes
- mike: add circuit-breaker on repeated CUDA_OOM per-instance (backoff + isolate)
- rita: follow up with affected customers with timeline and compensation.
rita (support): log ticket ids: TCK-9821 (customer-omega), TCK-9823 (customer-beta). ETA on final postmortem?
sara (eng-runtime): will draft P0 postmortem by EOD. include timeline, metrics, mitigation steps, and config diff.
jordan (oncall): thanks team. leaving a note in incidents channel and will hand off to next oncall at 2141600202. ack.
